question: With the same XGBoost-selected anchor and nominees, does the comparison among nomination rules carry over when both the guard and final predictor use a standardized logistic receiver? The original XGBoost endpoint results on these same tasks were known when this receiver replication was specified. Logistic results on these two slates have not been calculated.
cohorts: Use every layout and original selection in the locked first (10 tasks/30 folds) and wide (6 tasks/16 folds) panels. Keep them separate. Include singleton anchors with zero achievable compression. Keep all half-width candidates, original variable IDs, all exact original split memberships, label encoding and minority/AP indicators.
fixed_nominations: Use tree Gain, ordinal minimum vote, continuous full minimum and one-panel empty point as already sealed. Compare with exact uniform nomination over the same non-anchor candidates, paired with the identical downstream guard. For a singleton return the anchor. No proposal is redrawn. The receiver never enters nomination.
predictor: Independent per-support scikit-learn LogisticRegression with L2 penalty, C=1, unconstrained intercept, lbfgs solver, unweighted classes, tolerance 1e-6, max_iter 2000, float64, one thread. Multiclass uses multinomial loss. Fit training-column median imputation (keep empty features) then standardization (zero mean, unit variance) exclusively on the corresponding fit partition. Use the identical recipe on all subsets and data sources. In case of convergence warning, record support and iterations and keep the fitted result; do not modify settings or drop it.
stages: For every locked half-width candidate and the common anchor, fit on fitting plus proposal rows, predict guard rows, then refit from scratch on all development rows and predict outer rows. Save arrays, row indices, support list, original selection/layout/input digests and convergence information; seal all 46 folds before opening outer receiver outcomes. One deployed policy pays one candidate guard per actionable fold; the full slate is diagnostics only.
return: A nominee is accepted if its guard AUC and accuracy fall by at most 3% each relative to its logistic anchor, plus at most 5% relative AP loss in originally designated rare folds. Add 1e-12 metric slack. A guard rejection returns the logistic anchor. The same relative constraints define outer breach against the final logistic anchor on that fold. Safe compression U is deleted fraction of anchor width times the indicator for no outer breach.
estimates: Use binary ROC AUC, macro one-vs-rest AUC for multiclass, argmax accuracy and rare-positive average precision. Give each task equal weight after averaging its folds. For each panel, show U, breach, accepted deletion, AUC, accuracy, rare AP, all per-candidate guard/outer metrics and refit convergence. For exact uniform, average candidate-specific guarded final outcomes including reversions. Report full minus point, full minus uniform, ordinal minus Gain, point minus uniform, and point minus Gain with 30,000 equal-task paired percentile bootstrap draws (seed 33119). Give fold counts and the available hindsight joint ceiling as descriptive diagnostics. Intervals are exploratory. A separate label source is used for outer scoring. No tuning or new tasks after looking at results.
unavailable: Report any single-class scoring split, unmatched row/hash, non-finite outcome, incomplete fold or unavailable source. Abort on corruption rather than silently skipping it. Mark infeasible endpoints instead of imputing effects or adding substitutions. AP is absent on folds outside the existing rare-class criterion. Logistic learner has a different anchor baseline from XGBoost. This is receiver sensitivity within the same data sources and XGBoost-nominated feature slates.
